answer: Triangulate where agents run. Each epoch, five random validators ping every account and record round-trip times; real agents spread across a nebula of hosts and networks, while a sybil farm on one box returns near-identical latency fingerprints. Accounts whose fingerprints cluster share a single reward slot. Faking distance means renting separate machines in separate regions, so a farmer's cheap fleet shrinks to one ember of credit, and spreading it out costs as much as running real agents, from the tundra to the tropics.
